podcast.title: "Hey Let's Twist" Film
podcast.body: Joey D and the Starlighters starred in the film "Hey let's twist." The movie inaccurately depicted The Peppermint Lounge, where the band had their famous residency, as a family-run Italian restaurant rather than its true identity as a mafia-owned bar. "Hey let's twist, starred Joey D in the Starlighters, in a film which portrayed the peppermint lounge as a family run Italian restaurant rather than a mafia run bar."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Early Singles on Scepter Records
podcast.body: The group released a couple of singles on Scepter Records, with much of their material produced and written by Luther Dixon, who was a significant figure for the label. However, neither of these initial singles achieved particular success. "Neither of their singles on Scepter was particularly successful."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Interracial Band Status
podcast.body: Joey D and the Starlighters were notable for being one of the few interracial bands of their era, a characteristic that set them apart in the music scene of the time. "They were one of the few interracial bands of the time."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Joe Pesci's Early Career
podcast.body: Joe Pesci, who would later become a famous actor, was a rotating guitarist in Joey D and the Starlighters at one point. He also made a cameo appearance in the film "Hey Let's Twist," which was his first film role. "at one point including guitarist Joe Pesci, who would later become famous as an actor, rather than as a musician."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: New Jersey Live Popularity
podcast.body: Despite a lack of early chart success, Joey D and the Starlighters developed a strong following as a live act around New Jersey. This popularity allowed them to secure occasional gigs at various venues in New York. "but they became a popular live-act around New Jersey, and got occasional gigs at venues in New York."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Origin of The Young Rascals
podcast.body: The instrumentalists from the 1964 lineup of Joey D and the Starlighters eventually broke away to form their own band, The Young Rascals. This new group went on to have a series of hits between 1965 and 1970, marking a significant legacy from the Starlighters' lineup. "The young rascals, a group who had a series of hits from 1965 to 1970, started out as the instrumentalists in the 1964 lineup of Joey Dean the Starlighters, before breaking out to become their own band."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: The Peppermint Lounge Residency
podcast.body: The band secured a three-day weekend gig at The Peppermint Lounge in Manhattan, which proved so successful that they were offered a residency and became the house band. The small venue, with a capacity of about 200, became packed, largely with their 18-19 year old fans from New Jersey who were able to drink legally in New York (where the age was 18) but not in New Jersey (where it was 21). "Their shows there were so successful that they got a residency there, and became the house band."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: The Shirelles Connection
podcast.body: Joey D'Nicola, the band's leader, was a classmate of The Shirelles. When The Shirelles achieved their first hit, they advised D'Nicola to connect with Florence Greenberg, presumably to further his musical career. "Joey D'Nicola was a classmate of the Cherelles, and when the Cherelles had their first hit, they told D'Nicola that he should meet up with Florence Greenberg."
